newsitem.title: USA: CBOT traders say USDA data bullish for soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT traders say USDA data bullish for soybeans.

text.p: CBOT traders said the U.S. Department of Agriculture's monthly supply and demand report was bullish for soybeans, mildly bearish for corn and neutral for wheat.

Soybeans were seen opening two to three cents higher based a larger than expected cut in 1996/97 soybean ending stocks while a cut in estimated corn exports was seen driving prices down by around one to two cents at the opening.

Soybean 1996/97 ending stocks were cut to 180 million bushels, down from last month's projection of 210 million. The decrease reflected an increase of 30 million bushels to 900 million in USDA's soybean export projection.
"A little surprise in the bean carryover at 180, they were looking for 190," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Corn 1996/97 ending stocks were hiked to 1.157 million bushels, up from last month's 1.107 million due to a cut of 50 million bushels in the export projection to 1.900 billion.
"There was nothing much in corn or wheat, maybe a little bearish on corn," Kucha said.
USDA left unchanged its estimate for 1996-97 U.S. wheat carryover at 435 million bushels.

"They (USDA) did drop that (soybean) carryout a little more than expected, so we're going 2-3 (cents) higher. They dropped the corn exports by 50 million bu., so we're going 1 to 2 lower on corn," said Jason Roose of U.S. Commodities.
